intro: The platform APIs behind networking, observers, storage and workers.

entries.short: Promise-based, and it does not reject on HTTP errors.
entries.medium: The promise fulfils for any status, so check response.ok and throw yourself. Reading the body with res.json() or res.text() is a second await.
entries.detail: Wrap fetch in a helper that checks ok and parses the body, so every call handles errors the same way.

entries.medium: Pass controller.signal to fetch and call abort() to cancel, which rejects with an AbortError. AbortSignal.timeout sets a deadline, and AbortSignal.any combines signals such as a timeout and an unmount cancel.
entries.detail: Cancelling stale requests is how search-as-you-type avoids races where an older response overwrites a newer one.

entries.short: An older response can arrive after a newer one.
entries.medium: Abort the previous request when a new one starts, or tag responses with a sequence and ignore stale ones. Without this, a slow earlier request can overwrite fresh data.
entries.detail: This is a common bug in search boxes and filters, and it is invisible on a fast network.

entries.short: Know when an element enters the viewport.
entries.medium: The modern way to do lazy loading, infinite scroll and scroll reveals. It is asynchronous and computed by the browser, so it is far cheaper than a scroll listener that reads layout.
entries.detail: Set rootMargin to start loading before the element is visible, and unobserve once handled.

entries.short: React to an element's size, not just the window.
entries.medium: It works for any element, which is what responsive components need, such as a chart that redraws to fit its container. It replaces window resize plus manual measurement.
entries.detail: Guard against loops: resizing inside the callback can trigger another resize if you are not careful.

entries.medium: localStorage persists and is shared across tabs; sessionStorage is per tab. Both are synchronous, so large reads and writes block the main thread, and both store strings only.
entries.detail: The storage event fires in other tabs when localStorage changes, which is how you sync a theme or logout across tabs.

entries.short: An async database in the browser for volume.
entries.medium: It supports indexes, transactions and large structured data. The raw API is verbose, so use a wrapper such as idb or Dexie. It is the right choice when localStorage is too small or too blocking.
entries.detail: Storage is subject to quota and eviction. Check with navigator.storage.estimate and request persistence when it matters.

entries.short: Run JavaScript off the main thread.
entries.medium: No DOM access, so communicate by postMessage. Transfer ownership of large buffers to avoid copying. Use them for parsing, image processing or encryption so the UI stays responsive.
entries.detail: The main thread is where input and paint happen, so moving heavy work off it directly improves INP.

entries.short: A network proxy that enables offline and fast repeat visits.
entries.medium: It intercepts fetch events and can serve from the Cache API. It runs on HTTPS, persists independently of the page, and powers offline, push and background sync.
entries.detail: Version the cache and clean up old entries, or users get stale assets indefinitely.

entries.short: Messaging between tabs of the same origin.
entries.medium: Any tab can post a message and all others receive it, which is useful for keeping state such as a session or theme in sync without polling.
entries.detail: The storage event covers localStorage changes; BroadcastChannel is the general-purpose version.

entries.short: Deep clone values, including Maps and Dates.
entries.medium: It handles types JSON cannot, such as Map, Set, Date and ArrayBuffer, and preserves circular references. JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(x)) silently drops or mangles those.
entries.detail: It cannot clone functions or DOM nodes, but for plain data it is the correct deep clone.

entries.short: Build and parse URLs and query strings safely.
entries.medium: URLSearchParams handles encoding so you do not concatenate and forget to escape. It also makes it easy to add, read and remove query parameters.
entries.detail: Always encode user input in URLs. Concatenating query strings is how injection and broken links happen.
